ref: Νέος Ἑλληνομνήμων 16 (1922), p. 17 (printed page; running header Γρηγορίου Παλαμᾶ ἐπιστολή), PDF p. 9 of the Olympias scan. Sentence beginning «Διὰ ταῦτα τοίνυν».
url: https://olympias.lib.uoi.gr/jspui/bitstream/123456789/1865/1/doc.pdf (read via local copy O2/dl/nh16_1.pdf, PDF p. 9)
quote_orig: Διὰ ταῦτα τοίνυν ἡμεῖς πιστεύομεν τῷ Χριστῷ καὶ τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ αὐτοῦ, τὸν δὲ Μαχούμετ οὔτε παρὰ τῶν προφητῶν εὑρίσκομεν μαρτυρούμενον, οὔτε τι ξένον εἰργασμένον καὶ ἀξιόλογον πρὸς πίστιν ἐνάγον· διὰ τοῦτο οὐ πιστεύομεν αὐτῷ, οὐδὲ τῷ παρ' αὐτοῦ βιβλίῳ.
own_translation_en: Therefore we believe in Christ and in his Gospel; but Muhammad we do not find attested by the prophets, nor (did he do) anything strange and worthy of note that would lead to faith. For this reason we do not believe him, nor the book that he left. [Team translation, not a published English text.]
licence_note: Olympias PDF under CC BY 4.0 per the record (the scan). The 1922 Greek text is public domain by age. No public-domain English exists that I found, so the English above is my own literal translation.
keys: Μαχούμετ οὔτε παρὰ τῶν προφητῶν εὑρίσκομεν μαρτυρούμενον
τῷ Χριστῷ καὶ τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ αὐτοῦ
what_it_says: Palamas says Christians believe in Christ and his Gospel because the prophets attest Christ and he did remarkable works. Muhammad, by contrast, is not attested by the prophets and did nothing remarkable to win faith, so Palamas does not believe him or the book he left.
context: Palamas is writing from captivity to his own church in 1354 and reports debates with Turkish interlocutors (the speaker is Tasimanes, p. 16-17). This sentence closes his answer to the Turkish claim that Muslims accept the prophets, Christ and the Gospels while Christians reject Muhammad. The point rests on the criterion of witnesses (see pal_ep_02).
limits: Greek transcribed from the scan (no text layer). Word-level reading checked at high resolution. The Turkish side is known only through Palamas's report, so the argument is his summary, not a Muslim source. No public-domain English translation located.

ref: Νέος Ἑλληνομνήμων 16 (1922), pp. 16-17 (the sentence runs from the foot of p. 16 into the head of p. 17), PDF p. 9.
url: https://olympias.lib.uoi.gr/jspui/bitstream/123456789/1865/1/doc.pdf (read via local copy O2/dl/nh16_1.pdf, PDF p. 9)
quote_orig: Πρὸς αὐτὸν δ' ἐγὼ πάλιν, ἔθος ὑμῶν ἐστι καὶ ἡμῶν, ἐκ παλαιοῦ καὶ χρόνου καὶ νόμου βεβαιωθὲν, ἄνευ μαρτυριῶν μηδὲν παραδέχεσθαι καὶ στέργειν ὡς ἀληθές, αἱ δὲ μαρτυρίαι διτταί· ἢ γὰρ ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργων καὶ τῶν πραγμάτων αὐτῶν, ἢ παρὰ προσώπων ἀξιοπίστων.
own_translation_en: Again I said to him: it is a custom both of yours and of ours, established from of old and by time and by law, to admit nothing without witnesses and to accept it as true; and there are two kinds of witness: either from the works and deeds of the one in question, or from trustworthy persons. [Team translation.]
licence_note: As pal_ep_01. No public-domain English found.
what_it_says: Palamas sets out the criterion he uses: a claim is accepted only with witnesses, of two kinds, either the works and deeds of the person or trustworthy persons. The criterion is shared by both sides, so the Muslim claim must meet the same standard.
context: This is Palamas's own argument in the debate with Tasimanes, placed just before the reference to Moses, the prophets and Christ's works (p. 17). It is the method behind the verdict on Muhammad in pal_ep_01.
limits: Transcribed from the scan; the phrase continuing from p. 16 to p. 17 was checked on both page images. Argument is Palamas's account of the debate, not a Muslim source.

ref: Νέος Ἑλληνομνήμων 16 (1922), p. 17, PDF p. 9. The Turkish interlocutor's claim, reported by Palamas.
url: https://olympias.lib.uoi.gr/jspui/bitstream/123456789/1865/1/doc.pdf (read via local copy O2/dl/nh16_1.pdf, PDF p. 9)
quote_orig: Ὁ δὲ Τασιμάνης, δῆλος μὲν ἦν πρὸς ταῦτα δυσχεραίνων, ἀπελογεῖτο δὲ ὅμως λέγων ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ γεγραμμένον ἦν περὶ τοῦ Μωαμέθ, καὶ ὑμεῖς ἐξεκόψατε τοῦτο· ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐξ ἄκρας ἀνατολῆς ἐξελθὼν ἡλίου μέχρι καὶ τῆς αὐτοῦ δύσεως ὡς ὁρᾷς νικῶν κατήντησεν.
own_translation_en: Tasimanes, who was clearly annoyed at this, defended himself by saying that it had been written in the Gospel concerning Muhammad, and that you had cut it out; and (he said that Muhammad) went out from the far east as far as the sun's setting, conquering, as you see, and arrived. [Team translation; the opponent's claim, quoted by Palamas.]
licence_note: As pal_ep_01. No public-domain English found.
keys: ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ γεγραμμένον ἦν περὶ τοῦ Μωαμέθ
what_it_says: Tasimanes, the Turkish interlocutor, claims that the Gospel once contained a statement about Muhammad and that Christians removed it. He also points to Muhammad's conquests as evidence of his success.
context: Palamas reports this claim (p. 17) just before his reply that no Christian has removed anything from the Gospel (pal_ep_04). The claim is the Muslim-side argument that Christian Scripture was falsified, which Palamas rejects.
limits: This is the opponent's claim (Tasimanes) as Palamas reports it; it is not Palamas's view. The Turkish words are reconstructed only through Palamas's Greek. No Muslim source confirms the claim.

ref: Νέος Ἑλληνομνήμων 16 (1922), p. 17 (from «Ἐγὼ δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ἔφην») into p. 18 (to «προείρηκεν» and the start of «Ἀλλὰ καὶ πολλαὶ»), PDF pp. 9.
url: https://olympias.lib.uoi.gr/jspui/bitstream/123456789/1865/1/doc.pdf (read via local copy O2/dl/nh16_1.pdf, PDF p. 9)
quote_orig: Ἐγὼ δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ἔφην, τοῦ μὲν παρ' ἡμῖν εὐαγγελίου οὐδὲν οὐδέποτε παρ' οὐδενὸς ἐξεκόπη χριστιανῶν, οὐδὲ μεταπεποίηται τὸ παράπαν· ἀραὶ γὰρ ἐπὶ τοῦτο κεῖνται βαρεῖαι καὶ φρικωδέστατα, καὶ ὁ τολμῶν ἐκκόψαι ἢ μετασκευάσαί τι, τοῦ Χριστοῦ μᾶλλον αὐτὸς ἐκκέκοπται. Πῶς οὖν χριστιανὸς ἂν τις τοῦτο πεποίηκε, πῶς δ' ἂν ἦν ἔτι χριστιανὸς αὐτός, ἢ χριστιανοῖς ὅλως δεκτός, ἀποξέων τὰ θεοχάρακτα, καὶ ἃ Χριστὸς αὐτὸς ἢ ἐνέγραψεν, ἢ προείρηκεν;
own_translation_en: I said to him in reply: of our Gospel not one word has ever been cut out by any Christian, nor has it been altered in the slightest; for terrible curses lie upon anyone who dares to cut out or to alter anything, and he who does so has cut himself off from Christ rather. How then could a Christian have done this, or how could he still be a Christian, or acceptable to Christians at all, who scrapes away the God-written things and what Christ himself wrote or foretold? [Team translation.]
licence_note: As pal_ep_01. No public-domain English found.
keys: οὐδὲν οὐδέποτε παρ' οὐδενὸς ἐξεκόπη χριστιανῶν
ἀραὶ γὰρ ἐπὶ τοῦτο κεῖνται βαρεῖαι
καὶ ἃ Χριστὸς αὐτὸς ἢ ἐνέγραψεν, ἢ προείρηκεν
what_it_says: Palamas denies that any Christian has cut from or altered the Gospel, and says that doing so would cut the offender off from Christ. He argues that a Christian could not have done this, because the uniform witness of the many early Christian languages would have exposed it.
context: Palamas's reply to Tasimanes's claim that the Gospel was mutilated (pal_ep_03). The argument continues on p. 18 with the witness of many languages of the early Church (the Gospel was never written in one single original, and any alteration would have been noticed).
limits: The reply is Palamas's own argument in a debate that he reports. The words «ἢ προείρηκεν» are read from the scan (printed as προεἰρηκεν; scan resolution). Not a Muslim source. No English translation in the public domain found.

ref: Νέος Ἑλληνομνήμων 16 (1922), p. 18 (the sentence before «Ἵν' οὖν»; printed p. 18, lines 3-6 from the top of the page), PDF p. 10.
url: https://olympias.lib.uoi.gr/jspui/bitstream/123456789/1865/1/doc.pdf (read via local copy O2/dl/nh16_1.pdf, PDF p. 10)
quote_orig: Εἰ γὰρ ἐν τούτῳ γεγραμμένον ἦν περὶ Μαχούμετ τι χρηστόν, ἐν τοῖς προφήταις γεγραμμένον ἂν ὑπῆρχεν· εἰρῆσθαι δ' ἂν μᾶλλον γεγραμμένον καὶ μὴ ἀπολειμμένον, ὅτι ἐλεύσονται πολλοὶ ψευδόχριστοι καὶ ψευδοπροφῆται καὶ πολλοὺς πλανήσουσι.
own_translation_en: For if anything good about Muhammad had been written in this (Gospel), it would also have been written in the prophets; and rather it would have been said, and written and not left out, that many false christs and false prophets will come and will lead many astray. [Team translation.]
licence_note: As pal_ep_01. No public-domain English found.
what_it_says: Palamas argues that if the Gospel had said anything good about Muhammad, the prophets would have said it too. Instead the Gospel foretells false christs and false prophets who will deceive many. The implied application is to Muhammad, although the clause itself does not name him.
context: Palamas's argument against the Turkish claim that the Gospel once spoke well of Muhammad (pal_ep_03). The sentence inverts that claim: the Gospel's silence is the proof, and the prophetic warning is the description of the false prophets.
limits: The clause about false prophets does not name Muhammad; the identification is Palamas's implication. Two words are uncertain at scan resolution: a possible «καὶ» before «ἐν τοῖς προφήταις» (not read as present) and «ἀπολειμμένον». Greek transcribed from the scan; not a Muslim source.

ref: Νέος Ἑλληνομνήμων 16 (1922), p. 18 (the bottom of the page, from «Ἵν' οὖν μὴ τοῦτο πείθωμεν»), PDF p. 10.
url: https://olympias.lib.uoi.gr/jspui/bitstream/123456789/1865/1/doc.pdf (read via local copy O2/dl/nh16_1.pdf, PDF p. 10)
quote_orig: Ἵν' οὖν μὴ τοῦτο πείθωμεν, ὁ μὲν κορυφαῖος τῶν τοῦ Χριστοῦ μαθητῶν, ἔσονται φησι ψευδοδιδάσκαλοι καὶ ψευδοπροφῆται, οἵτινες παρεισάξουσιν αἱρέσεως ἀπωλείας καὶ ἐν πλεονεξίᾳ πλαστοῖς λόγοις ὑμᾶς ἐμπορεύσονται· πολλοὶ γὰρ ἐξακολουθήσουσιν αὐτῶν ταῖς ἀσελγείαις.
own_translation_en: So that we should not be persuaded of this: the coryphaeus of Christ's disciples said that there will be false teachers and false prophets, who will bring in destructive heresies and in their greed will trade you with false words; for many will follow their licentious ways. [Team translation.]
licence_note: As pal_ep_01. No public-domain English found.
keys: ὁ μὲν κορυφαῖος τῶν τοῦ Χριστοῦ μαθητῶν
πολλοὶ γὰρ ἐξακολουθήσουσιν αὐτῶν ταῖς ἀσελγείαις
what_it_says: Palamas quotes a warning attributed to the coryphaeus (leader) of Christ's disciples about false teachers who bring in destructive heresies and mislead many. He uses it to argue that the false teaching must not be believed.
context: Palamas's application of the warning to the teaching he opposes, which he presents as a false prophecy (see pal_ep_05). The page continues the debate with the Turks on the Gospel and their prophet.
limits: Palamas does not name Peter; «ὁ κορυφαῖος» is his description. The wording matches 2 Peter 2:1-2 in substance, but the identification with that verse is my own and the team should check it against the Greek New Testament. The Gospel phrase is paraphrased by Palamas, not quoted verbatim.

ref: Νέος Ἑλληνομνήμων 16 (1922), p. 18 bottom and p. 19 top, PDF pp. 10.
url: https://olympias.lib.uoi.gr/jspui/bitstream/123456789/1865/1/doc.pdf (read via local copy O2/dl/nh16_1.pdf, PDF p. 10)
quote_orig: Πῶς οὖν ὁ λέγων μὴ εἶναι ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ τὸν λέγοντα μὴ εἶναι κύριον τὸν διὰ σαρκὸς ἐπιφανέντα Ἰησοῦν, βιβλίον ἂν παρέδωκε, λέγον ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐλεύσεσθαι τὸν τοῦτο διαβεβαιούμενον· οὐκ ἔστιν τοῦτο οὐκ ἔστιν.
own_translation_en: [UNCERTAIN SYNTAX; provisional] How then can one who says that the one who says that Jesus, who appeared in the flesh, is not Lord, is not from God, have delivered a book saying from God that the one who asserts this will come? That is not so, it is not. [Team translation, provisional.]
licence_note: As pal_ep_01. No public-domain English found.
what_it_says: Palamas applies the 1 John test (pal_ep_08) to the Muslim book: one who denies that the Jesus who appeared in the flesh is Lord is not from God, so the book he delivered cannot claim divine origin. The exact syntax of the second half is unclear at scan resolution.
context: Argument continues from the 1 John test on p. 18. The Qur'an is not named; the book is the Muslim scripture in the Turkish claim (see pal_ep_11).
limits: Greek legible but the syntax is hard to resolve; «λέγον ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐλεύσεσθαι» is uncertain. The English is provisional. Palamas's book reference is probably the Qur'an but he does not name it here. Do not quote the English without the Greek.

ref: Νέος Ἑλληνομνήμων 16 (1922), p. 18 bottom, PDF p. 10. The sentence cites John's epistle (the «εὐαγγελιστής»).
url: https://olympias.lib.uoi.gr/jspui/bitstream/123456789/1865/1/doc.pdf (read via local copy O2/dl/nh16_1.pdf, PDF p. 10)
quote_orig: Ἔτερος δὲ πάλιν κἂν ἄγγελός φησιν εὐαγγελίσηταί ὑμῖν παρ' ὃ ὑμῖν εὐηγγελισάμεθα, ἀνάθεμα ἔστω. Ὁ δὲ εὐαγγελιστής, πᾶν πνεῦμα, ὃ μὴ ὁμολογεῖ Κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ἐν σαρκὶ ἐληλυθότα, ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ οὐκ ἔστι.
own_translation_en: Another (apostle) says: even if an angel should preach to you something other than what we have preached to you, let him be anathema. And the evangelist says: every spirit that does not confess the Lord Jesus Christ as come in the flesh is not from God. [Team translation.]
licence_note: As pal_ep_01. No public-domain English found.
keys: ὃ μὴ ὁμολογεῖ Κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ἐν σαρκὶ ἐληλυθότα
what_it_says: Palamas quotes the evangelist's test: a spirit that does not confess Jesus Christ as Lord come in the flesh is not from God. This is the basis of his reply to the Turkish claim to a book from God.
context: Given in the debate with the Turkish interlocutors immediately before pal_ep_07 (p. 18 bottom). The verse is 1 John 4:2-3; the identification is my own (Palamas says only «ὁ εὐαγγελιστής»).
limits: Quoted from the scan. The first sentence (Galatians 1:8-9 in substance; Palamas does not name the epistle) and the second (1 John 4:2-3, identified by me; Palamas says only «ὁ εὐαγγελιστής») are New Testament citations, not Muslim sources. The team should check both identifications against the Greek New Testament.

ref: Νέος Ἑλληνομνήμων 16 (1922), p. 19 (top, first paragraph and continuation), PDF p. 10.
url: https://olympias.lib.uoi.gr/jspui/bitstream/123456789/1865/1/doc.pdf (read via local copy O2/dl/nh16_1.pdf, PDF p. 10)
quote_orig: Ἐξ ἀνατολῆς δὲ κινήσας ὁ Μωάμεθ, μέχρι καὶ δύσεως ἡλίου διῆλθε νικῶν, ἀλλὰ πολέμῳ καὶ μαχαίρᾳ καὶ λεηλασίᾳ καὶ ἀνδραποδισμοῖς καὶ ἀνδροκτασίαις· ὧν οὐδὲν ἐκ θεοῦ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ προηγουμένως ἐστί, τοῦ ἐξ ἀρχῆς ἀνθρωποκτόνον δὲ μᾶλλον προηγούμενον θέλημα. Τί δέ, καὶ Ἀλέξανδρος οὐχ ἐξ δύσεως κινήσας τὴν ἀνατολὴν ὑπηγάγετο πᾶσαν; ἀλλὰ καὶ ἄλλοι ἄλλοτε πολλάκις στρατευσάμενοι πολλοί, τῆς οἰκουμένης ἐπεκράτησαν πάσης, οὐδενὶ δὲ τούτων οὐδὲν γένος τὰς ἑαυτῶν ἐνεπίστευσαν ψυχάς, ὡς ὑμεῖς τῷ Μαχούμετ.
own_translation_en: Muhammad, starting out from the east, went on conquering as far as the setting of the sun, but by war and by the sword and by plunder and enslavement and killings; none of which proceeds from the good God, but rather from the will that was a murderer from the beginning. Alexander too, did he not start from the west and subdue the whole East? And others, many, at various times, after many campaigns, won the whole of the inhabited world, yet none of them put his own soul's trust in their lineage, as you do in Muhammad. [Team translation.]
licence_note: As pal_ep_01. No public-domain English found.
keys: ὧν οὐδὲν ἐκ θεοῦ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ προηγουμένως ἐστί
τοῦ ἐξ ἀρχῆς ἀνθρωποκτόνον δὲ μᾶλλον προηγούμενον θέλημα
what_it_says: Palamas says Muhammad's conquests came by war and killing and are not from the good God but from a murderous will. He argues that conquest is no proof of truth, because others have also conquered without their trust being in their lineage.
context: Palamas's rebuttal of the Turkish argument that Muhammad's success (his conquests from east to west) proves his truth (see pal_ep_03 on Tasimanes's «νικῶν κατήντησεν»). The next sentence contrasts the spread of Christianity (pal_ep_10).
limits: This passage describes killing and conquest; it is a theological judgement and contains no exhortation to violence, so it is kept here under S (spread of Islam). It is harsh about Muhammad's methods, which the team may treat with care. The rhetorical question about Alexander is Palamas's.

ref: Νέος Ἑλληνομνήμων 16 (1922), p. 19 (the second part of the paragraph after pal_ep_09), PDF p. 10.
url: https://olympias.lib.uoi.gr/jspui/bitstream/123456789/1865/1/doc.pdf (read via local copy O2/dl/nh16_1.pdf, PDF p. 10)
quote_orig: καίτοι οὗτος, ὁμοῦ τε βίαν ἐπάγων καὶ τὰ καθ' ἡδονὴν προτεινόμενος, οὐδὲ μέρος ἓν ὅλον τῆς οἰκουμένης προσεταιρίσατο· ἡ δὲ τοῦ Χριστοῦ διδασκαλία, καίτοι τῶν τοῦ βίου σχεδὸν ἁπάντων ἡδέων ἀπάγουσα, πάντα τε περιέσχε τῆς οἰκουμένης τὰ πέρατα, καὶ μεταξὺ τῶν αὐτῇ πολεμούντων κρατεῖ, μηδεμίαν αὕτη βίαν ἐπάγουσα, νικῶσα δὲ μᾶλλον τὴν ἀντεπαγομένην βίαν ἑκάστοτε
own_translation_en: Yet this man, while bringing force and promoting pleasures of the flesh, did not win over even one part of the whole inhabited world; whereas the teaching of Christ, though it turns away from almost all the pleasures of life, embraced the ends of the whole inhabited world and prevails among those who fight against it, bringing no force at all, but conquering rather the force that is opposed to it each time. [Team translation; the text continues on p. 19 with the phrase «ὡς καὶ οὕτω ταύτην εἶναι τὴν νίκην τὴν τὸν κόσμον νικήσασαν», not included.]
licence_note: As pal_ep_01. No public-domain English found.
keys: νικῶσα δὲ μᾶλλον τὴν ἀντεπαγομένην βίαν
what_it_says: Palamas contrasts Muhammad, who spread by force and by appeals to pleasure, with Christ's teaching, which spread across the world without force and conquers the force opposed to it.
context: The paragraph continues the rebuttal of pal_ep_09. The contrast is part of his argument that conquest does not prove truth, and that Christian teaching prevails without force.
limits: Tied to the captivity narrative and the debate; a polemical comparison, not a systematic treatise. The text is read from the scan; the final clause of the sentence (p. 19) was checked at lower resolution.

ref: Νέος Ἑλληνομνήμων 16 (1922), p. 16 (the lines reporting the speech of Tasimanes), PDF p. 9.
url: https://olympias.lib.uoi.gr/jspui/bitstream/123456789/1865/1/doc.pdf (read via local copy O2/dl/nh16_1.pdf, PDF p. 9)
quote_orig: ὅτι στέργουσιν αὐτοὶ τοὺς προφήτας πάντας καὶ τὸν Χριστὸν καὶ τὰ τέσσαρα βιβλία τὰ ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ καταβαίνοντα, ὧν ἐστιν ἓν καὶ τοῦ Χριστοῦ εὐαγγέλιον· καὶ τελευτῶν ἐπιστρέψας πρός ἐμὲ τὸν λόγον, ὑμεῖς δὲ φητέ, πῶς οὐ δέχεσθε τὸν ἡμέτερον προφήτην, οὐδὲ πιστεύετε τῷ τούτου βιβλίῳ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ καταβάντι.
own_translation_en: They (the Turks) accept all the prophets and Christ and the four books which come from God, of which one is the Gospel of Christ; and at the end, turning the argument to me, you say: how is it that you do not accept our prophet, nor believe his book which came down from heaven? [Team translation; opponent's words as reported by Palamas.]
licence_note: As pal_ep_01. No public-domain English found.
keys: τῷ τούτου βιβλίῳ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ καταβάντι
what_it_says: The Turkish interlocutor Tasimanes states the Muslim position as Palamas reports it: Turks accept all the prophets, Christ and four heavenly books, including the Gospel, and they ask why Christians do not accept their prophet and his book from heaven.
context: This is the opening of the argument that Palamas answers in pal_ep_01 to pal_ep_04. It is the clearest statement of the Muslim argument in the letter.
limits: Opponent's view reported by Palamas, not a Muslim text. At scan resolution the participle «καταβαίνοντα» (or «καταβάντα») is not certain; the team should check the scan. The reference to four books is Palamas's report of Tasimanes's list.

ref: Νέος Ἑλληνομνήμων 16 (1922), p. 16 (the same speech of Tasimanes), PDF p. 9.
url: https://olympias.lib.uoi.gr/jspui/bitstream/123456789/1865/1/doc.pdf (read via local copy O2/dl/nh16_1.pdf, PDF p. 9)
quote_orig: Ὁ δὲ Τασιμάνης δοῦλός ἐστι φησί τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ὁ Χριστός.
own_translation_en: Tasimanes says that Christ is also a servant of God. [Team translation; opponent's view as reported by Palamas.]
licence_note: As pal_ep_01. No public-domain English found.
keys: δοῦλός ἐστι φησί τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ὁ Χριστός
what_it_says: Tasimanes says Christ is a servant of God, the Muslim view that Christ is not divine, as Palamas reports it. Palamas answers with the argument from scripture and Christ's coming in glory.
context: Palamas's report of the opponent's Christology, just before his own reply on Christ's role at the judgement (p. 16).
limits: SHORT QUOTE (11 words): the rest of Palamas's reply on the same page (about Christ judging the living and the dead) is only partly legible at scan resolution, so it is not quoted. Opponent view reported by Palamas, not a Muslim text.

ref: Migne PG 155, 'Dialogus contra omnes haereses', Caput XIV 'Contra gentes impias', approx. cols. 77-78 (page headers in OCR; verify on the scan). Latin facing text in the 1866 reprint.
orig_url: not available (Greek columns garbled in the OCR; Migne Greek not legible; no PD Greek reached)
own_translation_en: [Team translation of the Latin] He says that they were deceived by an impure and barbarian man who fell into demonic errors; he (Muhammad) called himself an apostle of God and claimed to have ascended into heaven, in rivalry with the Ascension of Christ our God; and he dared to say that he was above Christ and that he had seen God like crystal. [Insults in the Latin ('immundo', 'barbaro') are omitted from the paraphrase; see excluded.json.]
quote_latin: semetipsum dixit Dei apostolum, asseravit se in coelum ascendisse, ... Christi Deique nostri ascensionem, et semetipsum super Christum esse impia jactantia dicere ausus est, Deumque vidisse crystallinum ei splendore
licence_note: Migne 1857-66 (19th century): public domain. The English above is my translation (no PD English found).
what_it_says: Symeon says that Muhammad called himself an apostle of God, claimed to have ascended into heaven (as a rival to Christ's Ascension), and presumed to put himself above Christ by claiming to have seen God like crystal.
context: Caput XIV answers a cleric's question about the heresies of Nestorius, and then turns to the 'gentiles' (the Muslims). The Latin footnote identifies the subject as Muhammad. The passage is a doctrinal rebuttal of Muhammad's claims.
limits: No Greek quote. The Latin is from the OCR of the 1866 Migne reprint; the word 'indutum' and the verb before 'ascensionem' are not clear in the OCR and are omitted here ('...'). Insults in the same paragraph are not quoted (see excluded.json). The chapter is a Byzantine polemic, not a Muslim source; the team should check the Greek in Migne before publishing.

ref: Migne PG 155, 'Dialogus contra omnes haereses', Caput XIV 'Contra gentes impias', approx. cols. 77-78 (same chapter; verify on the scan).
orig_url: not available (Greek columns garbled in the OCR; no PD Greek reached)
own_translation_en: [Team translation of the Latin] They say that God exists, but they are wholly atheists, as before, since they do not know the true God nor confess the eternal Father of the living Word, unbegotten, maker of all things, ever-existing, nor the begetter of the living wisdom, the only-begotten and incorporeal Son, nor the Spirit, good and holy, who gives life and sanctifies all things. For these gentiles, seized by madness, reject the incorporeal Son and Word of God, and the divine Spirit who gives life that proceeds from him. [Insults and the sexual passage in the same paragraph are omitted; see excluded.json.]
quote_latin: Deum quidem esse dicunt, sed omnino sunt athei, ut prius erant, cum verum Deum non cognoscant, neque confitentur aeternum Verbi viventis Patrem, ingenitum, factorem omnium, semper existentem, viventis sapientiae unigeniti et incorporei Filii genitorem, sontemque verae vitae, boni et sancti Spiritus omnia vivificantis et sanctificantis. Nam hi gentiles amentia capti Filium et Verbum Dei incorporeum, divinumque ex eo et vivificantem Spiritum rejiciunt.
keys: neque confitentur aeternum Verbi viventis Patrem
what_it_says: Symeon says that the Muslims claim to acknowledge God but deny the eternal Father, the Son and Word of God, and the life-giving Holy Spirit, so that in his view they are atheists (the Trinity is denied).
context: Same chapter as sym_01. This is the sharpest doctrinal statement in the chapter: it moves from the Muhammad claims to the denial of the Trinity.
limits: Latin from OCR, with some letters doubtful: 'athei' is clear, 'atheoi' is possible; a few words in the OCR were corrected by me (e.g. 'vivificantem'). The insults and violence of the same paragraph are excluded (excluded.json). Translation mine. No Greek.
